paragraphs.text: Skeleton placeholder. Research CHFA Round One and Round Two Housing Tax Credit award announcements (2022-2026) for any City of Steamboat Springs project awards or denials. Verify against the CHFA awards index at chfainfo.com/rental-housing/housing-credit/awards and the per-round narrative PDFs.

Skeleton placeholder. Research the housing fund, dedicated revenue streams (lodging / STR / sales tax / mill levy), recent housing-strategic-plan adoptions, inclusionary ordinances, fee waivers, and council resolutions specific to City of Steamboat Springs.

Skeleton placeholder. Identify the public housing authority serving City of Steamboat Springs (municipal, county, or regional) plus any coalition memberships (e.g. WMRHC, CHA, APCHA, etc.). Document the authority's voucher inventory and any project-based vouchers committed to local LIHTC pipeline.

Steamboat Springs City Council chose in March to pursue a housing linkage fee rather than an inclusionary zoning ordinance. When staff presented final recommendations on Sept. 15, 2026, with four options for which residential and non-residential development would pay, council split on how, or whether, to move forward. Fee revenue would be limited to capital costs such as new construction and land acquisition.

The Affordable Ownership Need screening module recommends Rental + ownership mix for City of Steamboat Springs. It classifies rental pressure as Very High, ownership pressure as Very High, and counts 850 renter households earning 51–100% of area median income: the income range ownership programs usually serve, not a count of ready buyers.

The same screening run counts 1,046 renter households and 1,293 owner households as cost-burdened. This is a screening estimate only; verify local prices, financing assumptions, assistance programs, household size, and local deed-restriction policy before using it for a project decision.

Adopted plans. Housing Strategy and Action Plan (2024-2025) (adopted August 6, 2024): Recommendations aimed at preserving existing affordable housing and creating new affordable and attainable housing. Steamboat Springs Community Plan (Community Canvas) (adopted October 21, 2025): Comprehensive plan housing chapter targets 475 deed-restricted units to address catch-up demand.

Incentives and local funding on record: lodging or short-term-rental tax and housing trust fund. The Local Housing Incentives page has the terms and sources of each. Civic Readiness already credits its local funding, so the bonus does not count the fund records again.

Council and planning commission record. On January 21, 2025, the City Council approved: Ordinance approving an STR-tax grant agreement with the regional housing authority (YVHA) for Cottonwoods at Mid-Valley (vote 7-0). Grant for the development of affordable and attainable housing at the Cottonwoods at Mid-Valley project. On August 19, 2025, the City Council approved: Resolution approving STR-tax grant agreement with FV Basecamp, LLC (Lofts at Steamboat Basecamp) (vote 4-1). Operating subsidy for ten units for households earning 60-100% of Area Median Income. On November 25, 2025, the City Council approved: Ordinances approving purchase of the Campbell property with Short-Term Rental tax funds for affordable housing (vote 7-0). City land purchase, funded from Short-Term Rental tax revenue, for the purpose of providing affordable and attainable housing. On February 3, 2026, the City Council adopted: Resolution adopting the City of Steamboat Springs Affordable Housing Guidelines (vote 7-0). Adopts guidelines for the city's deed restriction program, including a pilot purchase-of-deed-restriction program. On February 17, 2026, the City Council approved: Ordinance approving Deed Restriction Purchase Program Agreements (vote 4-0). Approves agreements for the city to buy deed restrictions on homes, using Short-Term Rental Tax funds for a pilot.

In the Opportunity Finder this record adds a local support bonus of +4 of a possible +6 points as of October 29, 2026: plans +2, incentives and funding +0, council and planning commission +2. A part with nothing counted adds nothing; it never lowers the score.

The metric digest ranks City of Steamboat Springs at #4 with an overall housing-need score of 87.6. It identifies 372 deeply affordable units missing at <=30% AMI. The deep-affordability gap rate is 67.5% of <=30% AMI households. 61.4% of renter households are cost burdened, and 0.8% of occupied households are overcrowded.
Market and supply context: the digest reports a ZHVI market estimate of $1,313,950 and median gross rent of $2,017. 32.8% of households rent, and 36.8% of the housing stock is multifamily.

Demographics and demand: the population metric is 13,433. LEHD-based commuting signals show 6,815 in-commuters and a commute ratio of 58.1%. The digest's 20-year figure is 2,233 homes. Projected resident growth gives 1,519; it comes from the county projection, so read it as county context, not a place trend. Today's in-commuters give 714: homes for a quarter of the households, at or below 120% AMI, of the people who commute into City of Steamboat Springs, if they moved closer.
Opportunity context: the digest gives an opportunity score of 79.9 and a walkability score of 36.4. These are current digest levels, not trends.

Economic and service-worker context: the digest reports a workforce-housing pressure score of 77.8. A worker earning the containing county's LEHD earnings-bin wage estimate faces an ownership affordability gap of $292,838 and a rent affordability gap of $53,180. The county-context service-sector employment share is 36.8%, and county-context ACS cohorts show median gross rent changed 112.6% from 2009 to 2024 while median household income changed 47.1%. These county-context figures are economic context, not place-level sector or wage observations.
